title: Al Alam Palace

terrainReference.basis: Original terrain just outside the central palace frontage, within the ceremonial forecourt.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap Al Alam Palace building in named enclosure
mapIdentity.scope: OpenStreetMap way 66645876 is the mapped palace building in the separately named Al Alam Palace enclosure (way 66647557, Q2121461). The exact mapped outer corners remain controls. The long straight rear wall registers the heading; the two semicircular recesses in the central south edge establish the public forecourt side.

note: The original contractor Shapoorji Pallonji describes two long wings extending from a colorful cubic core. The National Museum confirms that the palace faces it on the ceremonial boulevard. Published firsthand descriptions report four flared entrance columns, two gold and two blue, under a broad roof. Recessed arches and an upright central flagstaff are represented at medium detail.
